title: Acute Myocarditis: From Pathophysiology to Risk-Stratified Management—A Clinical Review
one_line_summary: Comprehensive clinical review outlining the pathophysiology, risk-stratified diagnostic algorithm using CMR and EMB, and phenotype-driven management strategies for acute myocarditis.
key_pearls: **Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)** utilizing the updated 2018 Lake Louise criteria is the non-invasive cornerstone for diagnosis, achieving its highest diagnostic yield within **1–2 weeks** of symptom onset.

**Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB)** remains the diagnostic gold standard and is specifically **recommended** for fulminant presentations, advanced conduction disturbances, life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias, or lack of treatment response within **1–2 weeks**.

Targeted immunosuppressive therapy (e.g., high-dose **corticosteroids**, **azathioprine**, **mycophenolate mofetil**) is indicated for virus-negative, autoimmune, giant cell, eosinophilic, or **immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)**-associated myocarditis.

High-risk presentations and look-alikes can be identified using the **GRASP** mnemonic: **G**iant cell myocarditis, **R**elated to ICIs, **A**llergic/eosinophilic myocarditis, **S**ystemic immune-mediated disease, and **P**athogenic desmoplakin (**DSP**) gene mutations.

Uncomplicated myocarditis carries near-zero in-hospital **mortality**, whereas fulminant myocarditis with cardiogenic shock carries a **60-day** combined **mortality**/heart transplantation rate of approximately **28%**.

sections.heading: Introduction and Epidemiology
sections.content:
- Acute myocarditis is defined as an inflammatory disease of the myocardium without an ischemic, toxic, or traumatic cause, categorized by symptom duration into *acute* (**< 1 month**), *subacute* (**1–3 months**), and *chronic* (**> 3 months**).
- Global annual incidence ranges from **4 to 14 cases per 100,000 individuals**, with **60%–80%** of cases occurring in young adult males aged **20 to 40 years**.
- Most hospitalized patients (**~75%**) present with an uncomplicated clinical course characterized by near-zero in-hospital **mortality**, whereas overall population **mortality** ranges from **1% to 7%**.
- Chest pain is the most frequent presenting symptom (**up to 95%**), followed by dyspnea (**19%–49%**) and syncope (**5%–7%**).
section_pearls: Annual incidence is **4–14 per 100,000**, predominantly affecting males aged **20–40 years**.
Chest pain is the presenting symptom in up to **95%** of adult acute myocarditis cases.

sections.heading: Pathophysiology and Mechanisms of Inflammation
sections.content:
- Etiology includes infectious triggers (predominantly viral, such as **parvovirus B19**, **human herpesvirus 6**, **enterovirus**, **coxsackievirus B3**, **SARS-CoV-2**, and **adenovirus**) and non-infectious causes (autoimmune conditions, **immune checkpoint inhibitors**, and **mRNA SARS-CoV-2 vaccines**).
- The innate immune cascade is mediated by activation of the **NLRP3 inflammasome**, which processes pro-inflammatory cytokines **IL-1β** and **IL-18**, leading to macrophage recruitment, cardiomyocyte apoptosis, and electrical uncoupling via **Connexin 43** phosphorylation.
- Adaptive immune activation involves T-cell priming against viral and cardiac self-antigens (molecular mimicry with **α-myosin heavy chain**), driving cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell tissue injury and B-cell autoantibody production.
- Pro-fibrotic cytokines **IL-1** and **IL-17A** promote persistent myocardial inflammation, fibroblast activation, and progression toward dilated cardiomyopathy.
section_pearls: Viral etiologies have shifted from enteroviruses toward **parvovirus B19** and **HHV-6**.
Molecular mimicry involving **α-myosin heavy chain** triggers persistent autoimmune myocardial injury.

sections.heading: Clinical Presentation and High-Risk Phenotypes
sections.content:
- Clinical presentation ranges from mild chest pain to acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, and life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias.
- Conduction disturbances and high-grade atrioventricular block are characteristic of **cardiac sarcoidosis**, **giant cell myocarditis**, and **ICI-associated myocarditis**.
- The **GRASP** mnemonic identifies complex myocarditis phenotypes requiring specific etiology-directed therapies: **G**iant cell myocarditis, **R**elated to ICIs, **A**llergic/eosinophilic, **S**ystemic autoimmune/inflammatory disease, and **P**athogenic desmoplakin (**DSP**) mutations.
- Desmoplakin (**DSP**) gene variants present with recurrent myocarditis-like episodes and confer a **62.3%** 5-year risk of death, ventricular arrhythmias, or disease recurrence.
section_pearls: Use the **GRASP** mnemonic to screen for complex phenotypes requiring targeted treatment.
Pathogenic **DSP** gene variants carry a **62.3%** 5-year rate of adverse arrhythmic and structural outcomes.

sections.heading: Diagnostic Approaches
sections.content:
- Cardiac troponins are elevated in the vast majority of patients, accompanied by elevated inflammatory markers (**C-reactive protein** or **ESR**) in **80%–95%** of cases.
- Electrocardiography reveals abnormalities in **~85%** of cases, most commonly **ST-segment elevation** (**56%**), predominantly in **inferior** and lateral leads.
- **Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (CMR)** utilizing 2018 Lake Louise criteria (**T2 edema** plus **T1 mapping / LGE / ECV myocardial injury**) is the cornerstone non-invasive modality, optimal within **1–2 weeks** of onset.
- **Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB)** is the gold standard for histological classification (lymphocytic, giant cell, eosinophilic) defined by Dallas or immunohistochemical criteria (**≥ 14 leukocytes/mm²** with **≥ 7 CD3+ T-cells/mm²**).
- Novel circulating microRNAs (**hsa-miR-Chr8:96**, **miR-721**) and **soluble ST2 (sST2)** are emerging diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers.
section_pearls: CMR sensitivity is highest when performed within **1–2 weeks** of clinical onset.
Immunohistochemical diagnosis on EMB requires **≥ 14 leukocytes/mm²** and **≥ 7 CD3+ T-cells/mm²**.

sections.heading: Pharmacological Therapy and Targeted Interventions
sections.content:
- First-line management involves guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure in hemodynamically stable patients with reduced ejection fraction.
- **NSAIDs** combined with **colchicine** are indicated for perimyocarditis with preserved systolic function, but NSAIDs should be avoided in complicated acute myocarditis with heart failure.
- Empirical high-dose IV **methylprednisolone** is **recommended** by AHA guidelines in cases with high clinical suspicion of immune-mediated fulminant myocarditis prior to EMB.
- Targeted immunosuppression (**corticosteroids** plus **azathioprine**, **cyclosporine**, **mycophenolate mofetil**, or **tacrolimus**) is indicated for virus-negative, giant cell, eosinophilic, sarcoidotic, or autoimmune myocarditis.
- Novel immunomodulatory agents under evaluation include CTLA-4 agonist **abatacept** for ICI myocarditis, anti-IL-5 agents (**mepolizumab**, **benralizumab**) for eosinophilic myocarditis, and anti-IL-17A (**secukinumab**) for psoriasis-associated myocarditis.
section_pearls: Avoid **NSAIDs** in myocarditis complicated by left ventricular systolic dysfunction or heart failure.
Early combination immunosuppression improves transplant-free survival in **giant cell myocarditis**.

sections.heading: Non-Pharmacological Interventions and Mechanical Circulatory Support
sections.content:
- Mechanical circulatory support (**MCS**), including **VA-ECMO** and **Impella** (axial-flow temporary LV unloading), is required in **2%–9%** of patients presenting with cardiogenic shock or fulminant myocarditis.
- In peripheral **VA-ECMO** registries for acute myocarditis, nearly **two-thirds** of patients survive to hospital discharge, serving as a bridge to recovery or heart transplantation.
- The **2022 ESC Guidelines** recommend implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (**ICD**) implantation prior to discharge for patients with hemodynamically unstable sustained VT or VF during the acute phase.
- Wearable cardioverter-defibrillators (**WCD**) serve as an effective transient bridge strategy, with appropriate shock rates of **2.4%** and low inappropriate shock rates (**0.8%**).
section_pearls: **VA-ECMO** combined with LV unloading (**Impella**) bridges fulminant myocarditis to recovery or transplant.
**ICD** implantation is recommended before discharge for sustained unstable ventricular arrhythmias in acute myocarditis.

sections.heading: Recovery, Follow-Up, and Prognosis
sections.content:
- Athletes should abstain from competitive sports for **3–6 months**, though selective early return at **4–6 weeks** may be considered in low-risk cases with normalized LVEF and resolved inflammation on CMR.
- Biventricular systolic dysfunction and anteroseptal late gadolinium enhancement (**LGE**) on CMR are major independent predictors of overall **mortality** or heart transplantation.
- Post-discharge major arrhythmic events occur in **37%** of high-risk acute myocarditis patients, with **60%** of events occurring within the first year.
- Follow-up evaluation requires transthoracic echocardiography at **2–4 weeks** and repeat multiparametric CMR at **3–6 months**.
section_pearls: Biventricular dysfunction and anteroseptal **LGE** are the strongest predictors of adverse outcomes.
Standard physical activity restriction is **3–6 months**, contingent on CMR inflammation resolution.

sections.heading: Emerging Therapies and Ongoing Clinical Trials
sections.content:
- The **MYTHS** trial (*NCT05150704*) is evaluating high-dose IV **methylprednisolone** versus placebo in acute myocarditis with systolic dysfunction (**LVEF < 41%**).
- The **IMPROVE-MC** trial (*NCT04654988*) evaluates 12-month **prednisone** plus **azathioprine** in biopsy-proven virus-negative myocarditis with **LVEF ≤ 45%**.
- The **ATRIUM** (*NCT05335928*) and **ACHLYS** (*NCT05195645*) trials are assessing IV **abatacept** for ICI-associated myocarditis.
- The **CMP-MYTHiC** trial (*NCT06158698*) is testing **colchicine** (**1 mg** daily) to reduce myocardial inflammation in non-invasively diagnosed inflammatory cardiomyopathy.
section_pearls: Multiple ongoing RCTs (**MYTHS**, **IMPROVE-MC**, **ATRIUM**) are establishing evidence-based immunomodulatory protocols.

strengths_limitations:
- **Strengths**: Synthesizes recent guideline updates (2024 ACC, 2025 ESC) and contemporary registry data; provides practical diagnostic algorithms and mnemonic tools (GRASP); details state-of-the-art immunomodulatory trials.
- **Limitations**: Narrative review design without systematic quantitative meta-analysis; limited randomized controlled trial evidence supporting specific immunosuppressive regimens in viral-negative acute myocarditis.

drugs_doses.dose: High-dose IV bolus daily for 3 days
drugs_doses.indication: Fulminant acute myocarditis, severe autoimmune myocarditis, or acute heart failure prior to biopsy
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Hyperglycemia, infection risk, hypertension, fluid retention, psychiatric disturbances

drugs_doses.dose: 0.5 mg/kg/day orally (max 30 mg/day) tapered over months, or combined with steroid-sparing agents
drugs_doses.indication: Virus-negative inflammatory cardiomyopathy, giant cell myocarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis, ICI-myocarditis
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Adrenal suppression, osteoporosis, metabolic dysregulation, secondary infections

drugs_doses.dose: 1 mg daily orally (or 0.5 mg daily if weight < 70 kg) for 180 days
drugs_doses.indication: Myopericarditis with chest pain and preserved LVEF; ongoing testing in chronic inflammatory cardiomyopathy
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Diarrhea, gastrointestinal upset, leukopenia, myopathy, renal clearance adjustments required

drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Injection site reactions, neutropenia, serious opportunistic infections

drugs_doses.indication: Rescue and prospective therapy for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Infusion reactions, severe infection, headache, nausea

drugs_doses.indication: Steroid-sparing immunosuppression in virus-negative chronic myocarditis / inflammatory cardiomyopathy
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Bone marrow suppression, hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, malignancy risk

drugs_doses.indication: IL-17A-related myocarditis in patients with concomitant psoriasis
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: Upper respiratory infections, oral herpes, inflammatory bowel disease flare
